What Is Tungsten Eagle Testing With Its Liberty Ridge Drill Program in Nevada? - Kalkine Media
items.body: Highlights - Tungsten Eagle Development Corp. reported that first-phase diamond drilling is underway at its Liberty Ridge Tungsten Project in Elko County, Nevada. - The drill program focuses on the area where Union Carbide's historical drilling intersected tungsten and includes vertical holes that twin older holes. - Core is logged and photographed under ultraviolet light on site, with samples sent to ALS Global in Elko under a quality control program. Tungsten Eagle Development Corp. (CSE:MAGA) reported on Monday that the Tungsten Eagle drill program at the Liberty Ridge Tungsten Project in Elko County, Nevada, is underway. The first-phase diamond drilling campaign is designed to further evaluate tungsten mineralization that Union Carbide intersected during historical drilling and to characterize the geological controls on that mineralization. The update came in a company news release distributed through TheNewswire. The release serves as a progress report on a campaign that started in early October. According to the company, roughly half of the planned holes had been completed by late November, and the results are intended to guide the next stages of exploration on the property. How the Tungsten Eagle Drill Program Is Structured The release describes the first phase as a compact program of diamond drill holes planned to moderate depths. The final length of each hole can be adjusted as the core is assessed during drilling, which gives the geological team room to extend or shorten a hole depending on what it intersects. Harris Exploration Drilling Co. Ltd. is the contracted drilling company. Drilling is taking place from sites that have already been permitted, using existing access roads and prepared drill pads. The company noted that the number of permitted locations is larger than the first phase requires. That leaves capacity for follow-up drilling without starting a new permitting process for each additional site. Most holes are oriented to the east or west to cut across an apparent northerly trend in the target area, and they are drilled at an angle. The exception is a set of vertical holes designed to twin historical Union Carbide holes. Twinning older holes is a widely used exploration technique for testing whether historical intercepts can be reproduced with modern drilling, logging and assay methods. Union Carbide's Historical Footprint Defines the Initial Target The first phase is concentrated on the part of the property where Union Carbide's historical drilling intersected tungsten. The release states that those historical results have not been verified by a Qualified Person and should not be relied upon. Confirmation drilling therefore sits at the centre of the campaign, since modern core and laboratory data are needed before historical information can be used in any formal technical disclosure. Avrom Howard, Vice President, Exploration, led the team that designed the program. He said in the release that the primary goal is to document and characterize the mineralization, with more detailed drilling to follow where the results justify it. He also said the team is enthusiastic about having the work underway. Fiona Keating, Chief Executive Officer and Director, described the first-phase program as an important step in advancing Liberty Ridge. She said the company aims to build a clearer understanding of the project's tungsten mineralization and sees Liberty Ridge as positioned to contribute to American tungsten resources. Core Handling and Quality Control Behind the Assays Core logging and cutting facilities have been set up near the property. A geologist from On The Ground Exploration logs the core on site, and all core is photographed under both white light and ultraviolet light. According to the release, the ultraviolet photography is used to document scheelite and powellite, which allows the team to record visible mineralization before any sample leaves the site. After logging, the core is sawn in half. One half is sent for analysis, while the other half is retained as a physical record that can be re-examined or re-sampled later. Samples are shipped to ALS Global in Elko for preparation and multi-element analysis, with a separate method applied to samples that exceed upper detection limits. Certified reference materials, blanks and duplicates are inserted into the sample stream at regular intervals as part of the quality assurance and quality control program. Darcy Christian, P.Geo., an independent Qualified Person under Canadian mineral project disclosure standards, reviewed and approved the technical content of the release. Inside the Liberty Ridge Tungsten Project Claim Block Liberty Ridge consists of a sizeable block of unpatented lode claims covering a large area of Elko County. The property is reached by highway and sits entirely on land administered by the U.S. Bureau of Land Management, a setting that typically involves federal permitting for exploration disturbance. While Tungsten Eagle trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange rather than the Toronto Stock Exchange, sentiment toward Canadian small caps, often gauged through the [TSX Smallcap Index], can shape how companies at a similar stage are viewed. Tungsten Eagle has an option to acquire a full interest in the project from Silver Tungsten Discoveries Corp., subject to a net smelter return royalty. Option structures of this kind are common among junior explorers, as they allow a company to advance a project through staged work before completing its acquisition. The release also cites a Fraser Institute survey that ranked Nevada as the world's most attractive mining jurisdiction, and it describes Elko County as an established mining region with existing infrastructure and a skilled workforce. Those regional features can shorten logistics for drilling contractors and laboratories, which is reflected in the use of an Elko-based laboratory for this program.
